articleBlocks: At first, this looked more like a wellness shelf than a candle shelf. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Votive gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Aromatherapy and Unscented both fit that read, and they kept the board feeling broad instead of exact.
Birthday still did not belong naturally on a spa-products list.
Votive was the clue that changed the solve.
The moment I read Votive as a candle type, the earlier clues stopped drifting and started behaving like product names from the same aisle.
Aromatherapy became a scented candle. Unscented became an unscented candle.
Citronella then fit as the outdoor candle, and Birthday fit as the most familiar cake candle in the set.
The answer was Types of candles.
Once the answer lands, the board feels much tighter than any loose wellness-products read.
solutionNarrative: Aromatherapy and Unscented made wellness products or home fragrance items feel plausible at the start. That read held for a moment, but it stayed too broad and never explained why Birthday should belong in the same product family.

The turn came when I treated Votive as a product type instead of as just another lifestyle word. Once that clue exposed the candle aisle, the rest of the set resolved cleanly as specific candle types rather than as vague scent-related descriptors.
